Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

As a platform company powering businesses around the world, Stripe processes payments, runs marketplaces, detects fraud, helps entrepreneurs start internet businesses from anywhere, builds world-class, developer-friendly APIs, and more. Stripe’s engineering teams build the business logic that powers all of this. As a software engineering manager at Stripe, you’ll lead teams that build and expand APIs, services, and experiences. You’ll also work with partners to launch new markets and vertical capabilities.

Stripe Terminal helps our users extend their online presence into the physical world. The Terminal team’s mission is to make accepting in-person payments as easy as the Stripe API has made accepting online payments—enabling unified commerce. With Terminal, businesses can unify their in-person and online experiences, unlocking payment use cases that fit their business models—whether they’re creating a modern retail experience, extending a website to a pop-up store, or enabling mobile point-of-sale payments at an event.

Within Terminal, the Enterprise team enables our largest and most influential merchants to scale their businesses globally through:

  • Enterprise features, including in-person refunds, loyalty, and DCC
  • Enterprise-focused point-of-sale integrations
  • Vertical-specific payment methods, including SNAP EBT, Link integrations, merchant-specific QR payments, private-label credit cards and gift cards, and fleet fuel cards

What you’ll do

As an Engineering Manager on the Terminal Enterprise Features team, you’ll launch and scale merchant-specific features, build shared tooling for Terminal’s largest merchants, and partner with cross-functional teams across Stripe, including Go-to-Market, Legal, Design, and Product.

You’ll:

  • Partner with Stripe leaders across the company to create and advance the vision for Stripe’s unified commerce offering, bringing in-person and online payments together
  • Set the roadmap and priorities for your team and coordinate dependencies across the company
  • Support the engineering team in achieving a high level of technical excellence and stability
  • Develop processes that help the team do its best work and collaborate effectively with the rest of Stripe
  • Recruit excellent engineers in partnership with Stripe’s Recruiting team and develop engineers on the team, helping them advance in their careers
  • Develop a deep understanding of core Stripe APIs and influence their design to work effectively with card-present payments while building a platform for unified commerce
  • Empower and guide your team to build and scale integrations and core abstractions across payment methods, gift cards, and point-of-sale connectors for large enterprises
  • Deliver essential enterprise features such as DCC and in-person refunds

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in engineering leadership across mobile, API, and backend development teams, with demonstrated broad technical leadership
  • Experience building diverse teams to tackle challenging technical problems
  • An understanding of AI’s impact and a strong product mindset, with the ability to turn emerging capabilities into clear customer and business value
  • Experience thriving in a collaborative environment involving different stakeholders and subject-matter experts
  • Experience building and managing scalable, resilient, and observable systems across the stack
  • The ability to listen well, internalize the best ideas from across the organization, and set a vision that others are excited to support
  • The ability to put yourself in the shoes of Stripe’s merchants and users
  • Experience leading large technical projects with internal and external dependencies and impact across multiple teams

Preferred qualifications

  • Industry experience building, or managing teams that have built, in-person checkout experiences or payment-method integrations
  • Experience with in-person payment hardware and software, such as card readers and firmware
  • A deep understanding of the payments industry

Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But international fintechs and banks are left with two unsatisfying options to choose from: Either build on legacy correspondent banks that are slow and unreliable, or interface with middleware providers that neither move nor hold the dollars directly, but instead rely on underlying legacy banks themselves. At Augustus, we collapse the stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of ex-founders, founding employees of unicorns, and people who dropped out of university because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and Etched.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

As CDD Analyst at Augustus, you own customer due diligence end to end, from onboarding through periodic and event-driven reviews. You run CIP/CDD on individuals and legal entities, assign customer risk ratings, and run EDD on high-risk customers, complex ownership structures and FBO relationships. You prepare those cases for the High-Risk Customer Review Committee. You report directly to the Deputy BSA Officer.

We’re building an AI native bank, which is designed to run mostly autonomously. Legacy banks scale KYC with people. We scale it with agents, supporting human decisions. You improve the prompts of our review agents, and you work with Engineering and Product to automate onboarding within our regulatory bouunds. Your judgment sets the standard the agents follow. The goal is to make routine cases disappear so your time goes to the ones that matter.

Your First Six Months

  • Months 1-2: Work the queue yourself. Onboard individuals and legal entities end to end: CIP, document review, beneficial ownership certification and risk rating. Learn the Bank’s CRR methodology well enough to see where it’s unclear and where the review agents get it wrong.

  • Months 3-4: Own EDD on high-risk customers, complex ownership structures and FBO relationships. Your cases go to the High-Risk Customer Review Committee ready for a decision, with no rework needed. You’re rewriting agent prompts based on what you see in the queue.

  • Months 5-6: Agents handle standard onboarding and periodic reviews. You take the hard cases, event-driven reviews and exceptions. You work with Engineering and Product on the next onboarding flows to automate, within limits set by Compliance.

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

  • American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

  • Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

  • Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

  • Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

This role is for you if:

  • You reason from first principles. You ask what risk a check covers before you run it, and you drop the steps that don’t cover anything.

  • You don’t trade off customer experience. A clean onboarding is part of good CDD, and you never ask a customer for the same document twice.

  • You work hard. When the queue spikes or a case gets complex, you stay on it until it’s done right.

  • You challenge how things are done. If a process is slow, redundant or wrong, you say so, also upwards, and you bring the fix.

  • You’re diligent. Your files are complete, your reasoning is documented, and they hold up when someone checks them.

This role is not for you if:

  • You want a fixed checklist and a stable process. Ours changes every time the agents get better.

  • You see automation as a threat to your job. Here it is the job.

  • You treat CDD as box-ticking. An examiner may read every rating you set.

  • You need someone else to tell you a file isn’t good enough.

Hard Requirements

  • 2 - 6 years experience. Preferably at a top-tier consultancy (McKinsey, BCG, Bain), a high-bar startup, or as Chief of Staff to a founder.

  • You’ve been promoted or given a bigger scope faster than the standard cycle.

  • You’ve built automations, tools, or workflows that people use today (SQL, scripting, AI tools), not just recommendations.

  • Degree from a top-tier university.

  • Based in New York City and working onsite.

Pay transparency

Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate's experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is $100,000-$150,000 + equity.

What We Offer

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

  • Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.

  • Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.

  • Perks & Benefits: Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.

Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.

Augustus is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive and where different viewpoints and experiences are valued and respected. Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status.

About the role

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market, and trust in every account, deposit and trade is core to the product. As Head of Fraud, you will own Polymarket's fraud risk end to end: defining the strategy, building preventative and detective controls, and making sure every finding is resolved.

Your scope covers first-party fraud (customers abusing the platform themselves) and third-party fraud (bad actors targeting our users and systems, including account takeover). You will hold the bar for what good looks like both commercially and in the eyes of our regulators, and you will move fast.

You will partner with and influence Product owners and engineers you don't manage build and ship most fraud controls, so influencing them is critical to success in this role. You'll also work closely with Compliance, Legal, Data, Payments, Customer Support and Security.

What you'll own

Strategy and risk ownership

  • Own the fraud risk framework and appetite, and set the roadmap to deliver it.

  • Maintain a living fraud risk assessment and typology library across onboarding, funding, trading and withdrawals.

  • Report fraud exposure, losses, control performance and emerging threats to senior leadership and governance forums.

Preventative and detective controls

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to assess fraud risk before new products, payment methods, promotions, and material feature changes launch.

  • Define and implement controls that stop fraud before it happens: identity and device signals, step-up authentication, velocity and limit rules, and payment and withdrawal checks.

  • Build detective controls that surface fraud fast: monitoring rules, ML and AI models, anomaly detection, alerting and case management.

  • Tune controls continuously against loss rates, false positives and customer friction.

Fraud types in scope

  • First-party fraud: chargeback and friendly fraud, promotion and referral abuse, ACH fraud, multi-accounting, and identity misrepresentation by genuine customers.

  • Third-party fraud: account takeover, synthetic and stolen identities, stolen payment methods, phishing, social engineering, scams, and organized fraud rings.

Findings and resolution

  • Own investigations, from triage to root cause to closure.

  • Make sure every finding from monitoring, audits, regulatory exams and incidents has an owner, a fix and a deadline, and is closed out.

  • Feed lessons back into product, controls and policy so issues don't recur.

Team and partnership

  • Build and lead a high-performing fraud team of analysts, investigators and fraud data specialists.

  • Drive delivery through Product and Engineering: shape their roadmaps, win prioritization for fraud work, and design prevention into features from day one.

  • Work with Compliance and Legal on regulatory expectations, SAR-related escalations and exam readiness.

  • Select and manage fraud vendors and tooling.

What we're looking for

Influence is the most critical skill for this role, and we'll assess it at every interview stage.

  • Exceptional influence. You have a track record of getting fraud controls shipped by product and engineering teams you don't manage. You build trust fast, make a clear case using data, win prioritization against competing roadmaps, and turn disagreement into decisions.

  • Deep fraud expertise. 10+ years of experience in fraud within fintech, payments, banking, crypto, trading, online gaming, or other high-volume digital platforms, including at least five years in leadership, with direct accountability for fraud prevention, investigations, operations, and measurable outcomes.

  • Control design that works. A track record of building preventative and detective controls from scratch and proving they cut losses without hurting good customers.

  • Breadth across fraud types. Hands-on experience with both first-party and third-party fraud, including account takeover, identity fraud and payment fraud.

  • AI native. You use AI and automation as your default way of working: for detection models, investigation tooling, case triage and your own day-to-day productivity. You know where models beat rules and where they don't.

  • Commercial judgement. You understand that the goal is the right balance of loss, friction and growth, not zero fraud. You can put a number on the trade-offs.

  • Regulatory lens. You know what regulators expect from a fraud program (governance, documentation, testing, escalation) and can defend our approach in an exam.

  • Pace and ownership. You drive outcomes quickly, prioritize ruthlessly and close things out. You're comfortable in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

  • Data fluency. Comfortable working directly in SQL and with data teams to size problems and measure control performance.

Nice to have

  • Experience at a regulated exchange, derivatives venue or broker, or at a crypto platform with on-chain and fiat flows.

  • Familiarity with blockchain analytics and wallet-level risk signals.

  • Exposure to market abuse and trade surveillance, and how it intersects with fraud.

  • Experience building fraud capability across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Hands-on experience shipping LLM or agent-based tooling for investigations.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage
  • 401k match
  • Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories
 

Pay Transparency

Base salary range: $500,000 to $6000,000, plus equity and benefits.

This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe’s SMB Solutions Architecture (SA) team works with technical and business leaders (CTO/ CIO/ CEO/ Founders etc.), payments leaders and product engineering teams in the mid-market segment to evangelize Stripe’s solutions in the market. A solutions architect’s role is to build relationships with decision makers and think strategically about the business needs of Stripe’s customers. Solution Architects identify and propose Stripe solutions to solve complex business challenges and drive growth for our customers. SAs establish and prescribe best practices around a customer’s strategy, provide business and technical thought leadership and are viewed as a trusted advisor. They work on scaling business processes aligned to maximizing account coverage while working closely with customer and partner resources to deliver a solution that can be adopted quickly. 

What you’ll do

As a member of the team, the Solutions Architect will build highly consultative trusted relationships with c-level executives and technical decision makers in the customer’s organization to provide business and technical thought leadership, and become a trusted advisor in solving mission-critical business challenges. She/he will architect business models with them so they can drive new monetization opportunities and growth for both the user and Stripe. 

Responsibilities

  • Drive thought leadership and build executive relationships with key business and technical stakeholders including CIO, CTO, COO, CRO, CDO & Head of Payments. Strive to become their trusted advisor.
  • Work to deeply understand the customer’s business objectives and apply Stripe’s payments, SaaS, Banking-as-a-Service and Link Network solutions to customer challenges 
  • Secure the technical win for Stripe’s products by delivering demos, responding to RFPs, evangelizing Stripe’s products, and collaborating internally on narratives that align with the customer’s goals.

  • Collaborate with partners to help Stripe scale and reach its Total Addressable Market
  • Approximately 25% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way with users and collaborate internally

Who you are

An ideal candidate should have experience working for medium to large software companies (preferably in In payment-tech), focused on identifying business priorities, technology strategy, and solution design. They will have demonstrated the ability to become a trusted advisor to senior executives and facilitate customer success including business value identification(discovery/ demo cycles), road mapping, as well as advising and defining successful execution strategies.
